claim: To copy data to or from a self-managed in-cloud file server, or between AWS storage services in different AWS accounts, you launch an Amazon EC2 instance using a DataSync agent AMI.
question: When do I launch a DataSync agent on Amazon EC2?

values.display: launch an Amazon EC2 instance using a DataSync agent AMI

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync agent
qualifiers.condition: self-managed in-cloud file server, or AWS storage services in different accounts

evidence.quote: To copy data to or from a self-managed in-cloud file server, or between AWS Storage services in different AWS accounts, you launch an Amazon EC2 instance using a DataSync agent AMI.

claim: When you configure an S3 bucket for DataSync you can select the storage class DataSync uses, and DataSync can store data directly into S3 Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant Retrieval, Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Glacier Deep Archive.
question: Can I copy my data into Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval (formerly S3 Glacier), Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive, or other S3 storage classes?

values.display: S3 Standard, S3 Intelligent-Tiering

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, S3 as destination
qualifiers.condition: storage class selected on the S3 location

evidence.quote: When configuring an S3 bucket for use with AWS DataSync, you can select the S3 storage class that DataSync uses to store objects. DataSync supports storing data directly into S3 Standard, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA), S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA), Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, and Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive (S3 Glacier Deep Archive).

claim: DataSync stores objects smaller than the minimum charge capacity per object of the chosen storage class in S3 Standard, for example zero-byte folder objects that hold only metadata.
question: Where does DataSync store very small objects when the destination class has a minimum charge?

values.display: will be stored in S3 Standard

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, S3 as destination
qualifiers.condition: object smaller than the minimum charge capacity per object

evidence.quote: Objects smaller than the minimum charge capacity per object will be stored in S3 Standard. For example, folder objects, which are zero-bytes in size and hold only metadata, will be stored in S3 Standard.

claim: When S3 is the source of a DataSync task, retrieving objects from S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA incurs a retrieval fee based on the size of the objects.
question: Can I copy data out of S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA storage classes?

values.display: retrieval fee based on the size of the objects

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA as source

evidence.quote: Retrieving objects from S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA storage will incur a retrieval fee based on the size of the objects.

claim: Retrieving objects archived in the S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval storage class with DataSync incurs higher retrieval fees based on the size of the objects.
question: Can I copy data out of Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval?

values.display: higher retrieval fees based on the size of the objects

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval objects

evidence.quote: Retrieving objects which are archived in the S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval storage class will incur higher retrieval fees based on the size of the objects.

claim: Retrieving objects archived in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or S3 Glacier Deep Archive with DataSync results in an error, which DataSync logs and which gives the task a failed completion status.
question: Can I copy data out of Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive?

values.display: results in an error

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive objects

evidence.quote: Retrieving objects which are archived in the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class results in an error. Any errors retrieving archived objects will be logged by DataSync and will result in a failed task completion status.

claim: DataSync reaches an S3 bucket by assuming an IAM role that you provide; the policy on the role sets what the role can do, and DataSync can auto-generate the role or you can configure it manually.
question: How does AWS DataSync access my Amazon S3 bucket?

values.display: assumes an IAM role that you provide

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, S3 locations

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync assumes an IAM role that you provide. The policy you attach to the role determines which actions the role can perform. DataSync can auto generate this role on your behalf or you can manually configure a role.

claim: For NFS shares, the file metadata that DataSync stores in S3 user metadata is fully interoperable with File Gateway, which gives on-premises file-based access to the data DataSync put in S3.
question: How does AWS DataSync convert files and folders to or from objects in Amazon S3?

values.display: fully interoperable with File Gateway

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, NFS shares to S3, with S3 File Gateway

evidence.quote: For NFS shares, file metadata stored in S3 user metadata is fully interoperable with File Gateway, providing on-premises file-based access to data stored in Amazon S3 by AWS DataSync.

claim: When DataSync transfers objects between S3 buckets it copies the objects with their metadata and tags, but it does not copy object ACLs or prior object versions.
question: What object metadata is preserved when transferring objects between Amazon S3 buckets?

values.display: does not copy other object information such as object ACLs or prior object versions

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, S3 bucket to S3 bucket

evidence.quote: When transferring objects between Amazon S3 buckets, DataSync copies objects together with object metadata and tags. DataSync does not copy other object information such as object ACLs or prior object versions.

claim: With S3 on Outposts, DataSync can transfer data only to and from S3 buckets in AWS Regions.
question: Can I copy object data to and from Amazon S3 buckets on AWS Outposts?

values.display: only transfer data to and from Amazon S3 buckets in AWS Regions

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync with Amazon S3 on Outposts

evidence.quote: When using DataSync with Amazon S3 on Outposts, you can only transfer data to and from Amazon S3 buckets in AWS Regions.

claim: DataSync accesses an Amazon EFS file system using the NFS protocol, mounting it from within your VPC through elastic network interfaces that the DataSync service manages.
question: How does AWS DataSync access my Amazon EFS file system?

values.display: using the NFS protocol

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, EFS locations

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync accesses your Amazon EFS file system using the NFS protocol. The DataSync service mounts your file system from within your VPC from Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) managed by the DataSync service.

claim: Because DataSync mounts EFS file systems as the root user, your IAM policy must allow the elasticfilesystem:ClientRootAccess action.
question: How do I use AWS DataSync with Amazon EFS file system resource policies?

values.display: elasticfilesystem:ClientRootAccess

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, EFS file system resource policies

evidence.quote: Because DataSync mounts EFS file systems as the root user, your IAM policy must allow the following action: elasticfilesystem:ClientRootAccess.

claim: You can use DataSync to schedule periodic replication of an EFS file system to a second EFS file system in the same AWS account, in the same Region or across Regions, without a DataSync agent.
question: Can I use AWS DataSync to replicate my Amazon EFS file system to a different AWS Region?

values.display: does not require using a DataSync agent

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, EFS to EFS in one account

evidence.quote: Yes. In addition to the built-in replication provided by Amazon EFS, you can also use AWS DataSync to schedule periodic replication of your Amazon EFS file system to a second Amazon EFS file system within the same AWS account. This capability is available for both same-region and cross-region deployments, and does not require using a DataSync agent.

claim: DataSync supports NFSv3, SMB 2.1 and SMB 3 with FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and does not currently support NFSv4 or above with it.
question: Which protocol versions can AWS DataSync use with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP?

values.display: NFSv3, SMB 2.1, and SMB 3

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync with FSx for NetApp ONTAP

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync supports using NFSv3, SMB 2.1, and SMB 3. DataSync does not currently support using NFSv4 or above with FSx for ONTAP.

claim: DataSync cannot transfer data to or from FSx for ONTAP iSCSI LUNs; it copies only file data to or from FSx for ONTAP volumes using NFS or SMB.
question: Can I use AWS DataSync to transfer data to or from Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP iSCSI LUNs?

values.display: only supports copying file data

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync with FSx for NetApp ONTAP

evidence.quote: No, DataSync only supports copying file data to or from FSx for ONTAP volumes using NFS or SMB protocols.

claim: For a large migration you can partition the dataset across multiple DataSync tasks, which run in parallel and shorten the migration timeline.
question: How do I scale data transfers with AWS DataSync?

values.display: partition your dataset using multiple DataSync tasks

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync large migrations

evidence.quote: When performing a large migration, you can partition your dataset using multiple DataSync tasks. Partitioning your data across multiple tasks lets you run your data transfers in parallel and reduce your migration timelines.

claim: DataSync may slow other clients that use the same source data store, because the agent reads from or writes to it, and a bandwidth limit on the task reduces this impact by limiting the I/O against the storage system.
question: Will AWS DataSync affect the performance of my source file system?

values.display: Configuring a bandwidth limit for a task will reduce this impact

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync agent and on-premises source storage

evidence.quote: Depending on the capacity of your on-premises file store, and the quantity and size of files to be transferred, AWS DataSync may affect the response time of other clients when accessing the same source data store, because the agent reads or writes data from that storage system. Configuring a bandwidth limit for a task will reduce this impact by limiting the I/O against your storage system.

claim: All data DataSync transfers between source and destination is encrypted with TLS, data is never persisted in DataSync itself, and the service supports default encryption for S3 buckets, EFS encryption at rest, and FSx encryption at rest and in transit.
question: Is my data encrypted while being transferred and stored?

values.display: encrypted via Transport Layer Security (TLS)

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync transfers

evidence.quote: Yes. All data transferred between the source and destination is encrypted via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which replaced Secure Sockets Layer (SSL). Data is never persisted in AWS DataSync itself. The service supports using default encryption for S3 buckets, Amazon EFS file system encryption of data at rest, and Amazon FSx encryption at rest and in transit.

claim: A DataSync agent can connect to public internet facing endpoints, FIPS validated endpoints, or endpoints within one of your VPCs.
question: How do my AWS DataSync agents securely connect to AWS?

values.display: public internet facing endpoints, Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) validated endpoints

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync agent service endpoints
qualifiers.condition: chosen when the agent is activated

evidence.quote: You can choose to have the agent connect to public internet facing endpoints, Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) validated endpoints, or endpoints within one of your VPCs.

claim: AWS automatically applies updates to the DataSync agent VM, including the operating system and DataSync packages, once the agent is activated, non-disruptively when the agent is idle and not running a task.
question: How is my AWS DataSync agent patched and updated?

values.display: automatically applied by AWS once the agent is activated

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync agent
qualifiers.condition: applied when the agent is idle

evidence.quote: Updates to the agent VM, including both the underlying operating system and the AWS DataSync software packages, are automatically applied by AWS once the agent is activated. Updates are applied non-disruptively when the agent is idle and not executing a data transfer task.

claim: Use DataSync to migrate existing data to Amazon S3, and then use the File Gateway configuration of Storage Gateway to keep access to the migrated data and for ongoing updates from on-premises file-based applications.
question: When do I use AWS DataSync and when do I use AWS Storage Gateway?

values.display: use the File Gateway configuration of AWS Storage Gateway

qualifiers.scope: choice between AWS DataSync and AWS Storage Gateway

evidence.quote: Use AWS DataSync to migrate existing data to Amazon S3, and subsequently use the File Gateway configuration of AWS Storage Gateway to retain access to the migrated data and for ongoing updates from your on-premises file-based applications.

claim: After the initial DataSync transfer, File Gateway gives on-premises applications low latency access to the migrated data; with NFS shares, DataSync keeps the POSIX metadata of the source and the source permissions apply when files are accessed through File Gateway.
question: What does File Gateway add after a DataSync migration?

values.display: low latency access to the migrated data

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync followed by S3 File Gateway
qualifiers.condition: POSIX metadata preserved for NFS shares

evidence.quote: After the initial data transfer phase using AWS DataSync, File Gateway provides your on-premises applications with low latency access to the migrated data. When using DataSync with NFS shares, POSIX metadata from your source on-premises storage is preserved, and permissions from the source storage apply when accessing your files using File Gateway.

claim: If your applications already use the Amazon S3 API and you want higher throughput for transferring large files to S3, you can use S3 Transfer Acceleration.
question: When do I use AWS DataSync, and when do I use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration?

values.display: you can use S3 Transfer Acceleration

qualifiers.scope: choice between S3 Transfer Acceleration and AWS DataSync
qualifiers.condition: applications already integrated with the S3 API

evidence.quote: If your applications are already integrated with the Amazon S3 API, and you want higher throughput for transferring large files to S3, you can use S3 Transfer Acceleration.
